abstract: Protein-metabolite interactions are essential to numerous metabolic processes and underly many disease mechanisms. However, detecting these interactions is a challenge due to the transient nature of protein-metabolite associations. Here, we employ an untargeted functional metabolomics screening strategy to uncover low-affinity interactions between an entire metabolome and a kinase. We first utilize high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-guided fractionation to separate a whole-metabolome extract into multiple fixed-time fractions. A metabolite fraction library (mFL) of one-dimensional (1D) proton (1H) NMR spectra is then generated from these fractions. After adding the protein to the same fractions, saturation transfer difference (STD) NMR is then performed on each to detect weak protein-metabolite interactions and develop an STD library. Using the binding resonances from the STD library as a guide, the identity of the binding ligand can be determined. We demonstrate this strategy using frutosamine-3-kinase (FN3K) to identify and validate both known and novel binders. This workflow serves as a practical and simple way to screen an organism's metabolome for endogenous effector molecules, further strengthening our knowledge of protein-metabolite interactions and the functional metabolome.
